scenarios.title: Retire an unused socket and its service
scenarios.summary: Close an unused listener and its startup routes while keeping the required status service available.
scenarios.objective: Stop the obsolete import service and its activating socket. Disable the service and socket for future startup. Confirm the obsolete endpoint cannot answer now or after simulated startup. Keep the inventory-status service available now and after startup.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the current and saved settings separately before checking again.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: The service does the work. A socket unit waits for a request and can ask the service manager to start it. Use systemctl status on each supplied unit to distinguish a running service from a listening socket.
guide.action: Inspect the practice and assignment work orders.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Stop ends current operation. Disable removes the instruction to start later. Use disable --now to do both for one supplied unit, or issue disable and stop separately.
guide.action: Inspect the practice and assignment work orders.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: Test the obsolete listener before and after a simulated startup. Test the required status service separately, so a broad shutdown cannot satisfy the work order.
guide.action: Inspect the practice and assignment work orders.

scenarios.explanation: The obsolete service and its socket are off now and disabled for future starts. The required service still answers both requests.
hints: Check the .socket unit even if the .service unit is already inactive.
Disable changes startup enrollment. Stop changes the current session. The --now option does both in the supported command form.
Test the required endpoint before and after startup to detect an overly broad shutdown.
scenarios.simplifications: One source-held service/socket activation relationship and two supplied service endpoints. No real systemd, listener, process, host startup, arbitrary units, legacy inetd or TCP wrappers are used.

scenarios.title: Authorize a zone transfer by its verified key
scenarios.summary: Update a secondary zone copy using a verified key while keeping unsigned copies and an unrelated zone protected.
scenarios.objective: Apply a policy requiring an approved verified key for the served zone. Choose the matching current reference on the secondary. Refresh the secondary to its current serial and record. Reject unsigned and outdated proof requests without revealing a copy. Keep the unrelated zone closed for transfers and preserve ordinary authoritative lookup.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the current and saved settings separately before checking again.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: An address rule recognizes a source address. It does not establish that the sender and receiver share the intended credential. A DNS transaction signature (TSIG) lets the two servers authenticate their messages using a shared key.
guide.action: Inspect the practice and assignment work orders.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: The two hosts must trust the same key identity. An obsolete key with the same name fails the supplied authentication check. Use key references already provided in the exercise. Do not enter key material.
guide.action: Inspect the practice and assignment work orders.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: A successful transfer refreshes the older secondary. Read the new serial and address. Verify unsigned or outdated requests receive no copy, and ordinary authoritative lookups still work.
guide.action: Inspect the practice and assignment work orders.

scenarios.explanation: Matching current key references authenticate the approved exchange and the replica receives the published zone update. The unrelated zone and unauthorized cases remain protected.
hints: The served zone should require one of the supplied current key identities, rather than just the secondary address.
After editing, apply the policy and refresh. A correct rule alone does not change the old secondary copy.
Keep the unrelated zone transfer rule at none and verify the independent public lookup.
scenarios.simplifications: One supported allow-transfer statement per supplied virtual zone, opaque proof identities and real simulated serial comparison. No MAC/key generation, packets, time verification, full BIND syntax, real DNS, DNSSEC, DANE or root/jail setup is simulated.
